plan.estimand: Mean increase in normally distributed outcome
plan.hypothesis: One-sample mean shift from null (0) to 0.2 units
assumptions: Population standard deviation equals sample standard deviation (0.5)
scientific_notes: One-sided test: H0: μ ≤ 0 vs H1: μ > 0
Critical value from one-sided t-distribution with df=24 at α=0.05

answer.summary: For a one-sided one-sample t-test at significance level α = 0.05, detecting a mean increase of 0.2 units with standard deviation 0.5 in a normally distributed outcome with n = 25 participants, the statistical power is 0.6173 (61.73%).
answer.method: One-sample t-test with non-central t-distribution. Effect size Cohen's d = mean difference / SD = 0.2 / 0.5 = 0.4. Non-centrality parameter λ = d × √n = 0.4 × √25 = 2.0. Under H₁ (true mean = 0.2), the test statistic follows a non-central t-distribution with df = 24 and ncp = 2.0. The critical value for a one-sided right-tailed test at α = 0.05 is t_crit = 1.7109. Power = P(T > 1.7109 | H₁) = 1 − Pr(T ≤ 1.7109; df=24, ncp=2.0) = 0.6173. Calculated and verified using pwr::pwr.t.test.
assumptions: Observations are independent and identically distributed
One-sided hypothesis: H₀: μ ≤ 0 vs H₁: μ > 0
True population mean under the alternative is 0.2
limitations: Power depends critically on the assumed SD = 0.5; if actual SD differs, achieved power will differ materially
Assumes normal distribution of the outcome; violations affect actual power
Does not account for loss to follow-up, non-compliance, or other practical deviations
One-sided test requires pre-specification of directionality

# One-sample t-test power calculation
# H0: mu <= 0 vs H1: mu > 0 (one-sided, right-tailed)
# H0: mu = 0 under null
# HA: mu = 0.2 under alternative

n <- 25
alpha <- 0.05
mean_diff <- 0.2
sd <- 0.5
df <- n - 1

# Effect size (Cohen's d)
cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd
cat("Cohen's d =", cohens_d, "\n")

# Non-centrality parameter
ncp <- cohens_d * sqrt(n)
cat("Non-centrality parameter =", ncp, "\n")

# Critical value for one-sided test
# For one-sided, we use the upper quantile at alpha level
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
cat("Critical t-value (one-sided, alpha=0.05, df=24) =", t_crit, "\n")

# Power = P(T > t_crit | H1 true)
# When H1 is true, the test statistic follows non-central t distribution
# with ncp = 2.0 and df = 24
power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = ncp)

cat("\nPower calculation:\n")
cat("Power = P(T >", t_crit, "| H1 true)\n")
cat("Power =", power, "\n")

# Verification using power.t.test (which uses same approach for one-sample)
library_check <- requireNamespace("stats", quietly = TRUE)
ptt <- power.t.test(n = n, delta = mean_diff, sd = sd, 
                     sig.level = alpha, type = "one.sample",
                     alternative = "one.sided")
cat("\nVerification with power.t.test:\n")
cat("Power =", ptt$power, "\n")

# Final result
cat("\n=== RESULT ===\n")
cat("Power (probability) =", power, "\n")

# Output in required format
result <- list(
  metric = "power",
  value = power,
  unit = "probability"
)
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = list(result)), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n", sep = "")

# One-sample t-test power: one-sided, alpha=0.05, n=25, delta=0.2, sd=0.5
library(pwr)

# Parameters
n <- 25
delta <- 0.2        # mean difference
sd <- 0.5          # standard deviation
alpha <- 0.05      # significance level
cohens_d <- delta / sd  # = 0.4

# Calculate power
power <- pwr.t.test(
  n = n,
  d = cohens_d,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "one.sample",
  alternative = "greater"
)$power

# Verify with manual calculation
df <- n - 1
ncp <- cohens_d * sqrt(n)
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
power_manual <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = ncp)

cat("Computed power (pwr package):", power, "\n")
cat("Computed power (manual):", power_manual, "\n")
cat("These should match:", all.equal(power, power_manual), "\n")

# Express as decimal in multiple formats for verification
cat("\nDecimal representations:\n")
cat(sprintf("%.6f\n", power))
cat(sprintf("%.10f\n", power))
cat(sprintf("%.15f\n", power))

# Output for validation
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(results = list(
    list(metric = "power", value = power, unit = "probability")
